subject: reading
studentMessage: I'm reading and there's a word I don't know. There's a picture of a dog next to it, so is the word 'dog'?
rubric: Redirects away from guessing the word from the picture (rejects three-cueing)
Guides decoding by letters and sounds instead
Does not simply tell the child the word
Ends with a concrete next move (a sound or step to try)
Warm and simple language for a young child

subject: reading
studentMessage: The letters are s, u, n. I see /s/ /u/ /n/ but I don't get what the word is.
rubric: Diagnoses that the child has the sounds but needs to blend them
Guides blending the sounds together rather than stating the word
Gives a concrete blending move (e.g. say the sounds faster/connected)
Does not give the final word outright
Encouraging tone for an early reader

subject: reading
studentMessage: I just look at the first letter and then guess a word that would make sense in the sentence. That's how I read tricky words.
rubric: Identifies guessing-from-first-letter-and-context as the wrong strategy (three-cueing misconception)
Teaches reading all the letters/sounds left to right and blending
Addresses the misconception directly rather than ignoring it
Leaves the child with a better strategy to try
Stays warm and not shaming

subject: reading
studentMessage: What is the first sound in the word 'map'? I think it might be 'em' like the letter name.
rubric: Recognizes the confusion between letter NAME (em) and letter SOUND (/m/)
Works on the first sound orally (phonemic awareness)
Guides the child to the sound rather than just announcing it
Gives a next move to try the sound
Simple, playful, age-appropriate

subject: reading
studentMessage: The word is 'said'. I tried to sound it out s-a-i-d but it sounded wrong and I gave up.
rubric: Praises that sounding out was the right instinct
Explains the tricky part of the word in a kid-friendly way rather than just giving it
Does not tell the child to guess from a picture or context
Gives the child a concrete next step
Warm and reassuring after the child gave up

subject: reading
studentMessage: I read the sentence 'The wet dog shook by the door.' but I don't know why the dog is wet.
rubric: Treats this as comprehension (meaning), since the words are already decoded
Asks a question or points to text evidence rather than just explaining
Builds understanding step by step
Leaves the child with something to think about or try
Encouraging and age-appropriate
